related_questions.question: Why are so many people getting COVID-19 again?
related_questions.snippet: Once you have had COVID-19, your immune system responds in several ways. This immune response can protect you against reinfection for several months, but this protection decreases over time. People with weakened immune systems who get an infection may have a limited immune response or none at all.
related_questions.title: About Reinfection | COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: How serious is catching COVID-19 now?
related_questions.snippet: Many people with COVID-19, also called coronavirus disease 2019, recover at home. But for some, COVID-19 can be a serious illness. Some people may need care in the hospital, treatment in the intensive care unit and the need for breathing help. In some people, severe COVID-19 illness can lead to death.
related_questions.title: COVID-19: Who's at higher risk of serious symptoms? - Mayo Clinic

related_questions.question: How many days from exposure will I get COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Key points. People with COVID-19 have a wide range of symptoms ranging from mild symptoms to severe illness. Symptoms may appear 2-14 days after exposure to the virus. Symptoms may start as mild, and some people will progress to more severe symptoms.
related_questions.title: Symptoms of COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: Is long covid increasing or decreasing?
related_questions.snippet: While data are limited, the chance of developing post COVID-19 condition appears to be lower now than earlier in the pandemic. However, the virus is still circulating widely, and every new infection is associated with a risk.
